title: Circular Measure Module 4 Lesson 1: Non-Overlapping Intersecting & Adjacent Sectors custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values and combinations are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs scope and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Two identical circles, each of radius $6\text{ cm}$, pass through each other's centres, so the distance between their centres is $6\text{ cm}$. Find the exact angle in radians subtended at either centre in the triangle formed by the two centres and one intersection point.

Two circles of radii $7\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ have centres $A$ and $B$ that are $9\text{ cm}$ apart, and they intersect at point $C$. Use the cosine rule to find the exact value of $\cos(\angle CAB)$.

Two identical circles of radius $10\text{ cm}$ have centres $A$ and $B$ which are $12\text{ cm}$ apart, and intersect at points $C$ and $D$. By bisecting the isosceles triangle $\triangle ABC$, find the exact value of $\cos\theta$, where $\theta = \angle CAB$ is the half-angle at centre $A$.
Two identical circles of radius $10\text{ cm}$ have centres $12\text{ cm}$ apart and intersect at $C$ and $D$. Find the exact length of the common chord $CD$.

Two identical circles of radius $6\text{ cm}$ have centres $6\text{ cm}$ apart and intersect. Given that the angle subtended by the common chord at each centre is $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$, find the exact area of the single minor segment of one circle cut off by the common chord.

Two identical circles of radius $6\text{ cm}$ have centres $6\text{ cm}$ apart. The region of overlap is a lens bounded by two congruent circular arcs, each subtended by a central angle of $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$. Find the exact perimeter of this lens.

Two circles of radii $5\text{ cm}$ and $4\text{ cm}$ have centres $7\text{ cm}$ apart and intersect. Find the angle at the radius-$5$ centre in the triangle formed by the centres and one intersection point.
